A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices for the same DML-IL research. The changed title and reorganized appendices do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original experiments on ticket pricing and modified MuJoCo environments, measuring imitation error and reward.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a confounding-horizon misspecification experiment in Appendix C.2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same Gaussian-mixture rollout model, policy-learning procedure, and cross-fitting. The architecture table is unchanged. Added discussion of DML-CMR and discrete actions does not revise the specified algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ticket pricing, Ant, Half Cheetah, and Hopper with the same task definitions. The new misspecification study reuses existing environments and changes the supplied algorithm parameter, rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Main comparisons retain BC, BC-SEQ, ResiduIL, and the noised expert. The ticket-pricing and Ant solver comparisons retain DFIV and DeepGMM. Newly discussed methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a controlled protocol fixing the true confounding horizon at 10 while supplying DML-IL with k=1 through 9, alongside a correctly specified k=10 control. Existing training budgets, architectures, metrics, and 50-episode evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis testing how underestimating the confounding horizon affects DML-IL on Half Cheetah and ticket pricing. Existing horizon-strength sweeps and alternative-solver analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard-deviation bands for existing results. The new table also reports standard deviations, continuing the same uncertainty-reporting practice. No new seed counts, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Existing Figures 2–5 retain identical plot images. New Table 1 reports rewards under horizon misspecification: Half Cheetah changes from 0.7183 at supplied k=10 to 0.0896 at k=1, and ticket pricing from 0.6181 to 0.0656. These are added sensitivity results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a d-separation argument for instrument validity beyond v1's brief check. Appendix G specifies orthogonality, identifiability, and an o(N^-1/4) nuisance-estimation requirement for the retained root-N convergence claim. The principal assumptions, imitation-gap bounds, and existing proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and rewritten summaries, both versions claim a framework combining expert-observable and expert-unobservable confounding, a history-based CMR formulation, DML-IL, imitation-gap bounds recovering prior results, and empirical superiority over the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and failure-condition discussion in Sections 4.1 and 6 and Appendices C and F. Beyond v1's existing horizon and additivity caveats, it discusses continuous-action restrictions, non-additive-noise failures, healthcare limitations, indirect instrument diagnostics, invalid-instrument bias, and weak-instrument explanations for solver instability.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly discloses Ubuntu 18.04.2, two Intel Xeon Gold 6252 CPUs, and one RTX 2080 Ti GPU per experiment run. Existing architecture, optimizer, training-budget, environment-processing, and evaluation details are retained; this disclosure does not establish changed hardware or rerun experiments.

R1.justification: V2 broadens positioning through an explicit contrast with Ruan et al. (2024) on partial identification, discussion of invalid-instrument synthesis and diagnostic literature, and a connection to DML-CMR from Shao et al. (2025). These additions explain how the work's assumptions and guarantees relate to several previously undiscussed research directions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, explanatory passages in Sections 3–4 are reordered, and Conclusion becomes Discussion. Appendices are substantially reorganized: alternative-solver experiments move into C, environment and implementation details shift, and cross-fitting material moves into G.

P2.justification: The main visual presentation is substantially reorganized. Figures 1–3 are enlarged, and Figure 3 changes from two rows of three plots to three task-paired rows of two. Appendix figures are relocated and compacted, a sensitivity table is added, and the unchanged architecture table becomes Table 2.

improvement.justification: The added misspecification experiment, fuller applicability discussion, hardware disclosure, and more readable figures improve practical scrutiny and transparency. The gains remain limited because selecting the horizon is unresolved, and the new results are overstated in one passage: Appendix C.2 claims Half Cheetah stays within 5% down to k=6, but Table 1's k=7 reward of 0.6675 is about 7.1% below the 0.7183 control.
